digest.lead: Anthropic filed for a public offering today, marking a potential watershed moment for the AI industry as one of the major players prepares to go public.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code received important security updates and Stanford published AI agent guidelines highlighting Claude's role in academic settings.

stories.headline: Anthropic Files for IPO, Releases New Claude Opus Model
stories.summary: Anthropic filed confidential S1 documents with the SEC for a public offering [1][2], while also announcing a new Series H funding round [3] and releasing Claude Opus 4.8 [4]. The IPO filing has generated significant discussion about whether public markets can absorb major AI companies [5].
key_points: First major AI company to file for public offering after OpenAI speculation
Concurrent Series H funding suggests strong investor interest ahead of IPO
New Opus model release timed with corporate milestone announcements
stories.impact: This IPO could set valuation benchmarks for the entire AI industry and provide public market access to Claude AI technology for institutional investors.

sources.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O.
Can the stockmarket swallow Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI?

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.160 Adds Security Prompts for System File Modifications
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release introduces safety prompts before modifying shell startup files and build tool configurations [1]. The update also streamlines the editing workflow by eliminating the need for separate read operations after grep commands [1].
key_points: New prompts prevent accidental execution through shell startup file modifications
Build tool config files now require explicit confirmation in acceptEdits mode
Improved grep workflow reduces friction for single-file operations
stories.impact: These security improvements make Claude Code safer for developers working in production environments while maintaining development velocity.

stories.headline: Stanford CS336 Course Adopts Claude with Detailed AI Agent Guidelines
stories.summary: Stanford's CS336 course published comprehensive guidelines for using Claude as an AI agent in academic assignments [1]. The documentation has gained significant attention from the developer community, highlighting Claude's growing role in computer science education [1].
stories.impact: This formal adoption by a prestigious CS program could accelerate Claude's integration into academic curricula and establish best practices for AI-assisted learning.

stories.headline: Enable acceptEdits mode for safer file modifications in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.160 introduced enhanced safety prompts in acceptEdits mode that warn before writing to potentially dangerous files like shell startup files and build configs. This prevents unintended command execution while still allowing necessary edits.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.160 or later
Enable acceptEdits mode in your Claude Code configuration
Review and approve prompts when Claude attempts to edit shell startup files or build configs
Test that the safety prompts appear when editing files like .zshenv, .npmrc, or .pre-commit-config.yaml

stories.headline: Use `/code-review` with effort levels for better code analysis
stories.summary: The `/simplify` command has been renamed to `/code-review` and now accepts optional effort levels like 'high' for more thorough analysis. This gives you better control over how deeply Claude examines your code for potential improvements.
actionable_steps: Add effort levels like `/code-review high` for more thorough analysis
Use `/code-review low` for quick reviews or `/code-review medium` for standard analysis

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to extend prompt cache duration
stories.summary: Setting this environment variable enables 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default, which can reduce API costs and improve response times for longer coding sessions. This works across API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry deployments.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=true in your system or deployment configuration
Restart Claude Code to apply the new caching setting
Monitor your usage to verify extended caching is working

stories.headline: Configure worktree base reference to preserve unpushed commits
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code update changed the default behavior for worktrees to branch from origin instead of local HEAD, potentially losing unpushed commits. Setting the baseRef to 'head' preserves your local work when creating new worktrees.
